questions.solution_html:
• Mention one advantage of sex reversal in fishes
  • Production of Monosex Populations 2. Faster Growth Rate, 3. Prevention of
  • Unwanted Breeding, 4. Better Feed Utilization, 5. Uniform Size and Quality, 6.
  • Increased Yield and Profit, 7. Efficient Use of Culture Systems, 8. Control Over
  • Breeding Programs (mention any one)
  • Sex is fixed by sex chromosomes or specific genes inherited from parents.
  • It is similar to mechanisms seen in other animals, where combinations like

questions.question: Mention the sexual dimorphism between male and female Amia calva.

  • males: stimulates spermiation, Triggers spawning behavior

questions.question: What is Gonadotropin Releasing Inhibitory Factor?
questions.solution_html:
• Gonadotropin Releasing Inhibitory Factor (GRIF) is a neuropeptide hormone that
  • suppresses reproductive activity. It is a hormone produced in the hypothalamus that
  • inhibits the release of gonadotropins from the pituitary gland. Eg. Dopamine
  • Function – Secretes thyroid hormones (T₃, T₄); regulates metabolism, growth
  • metamorphosis, osmoregulation
  • Ultimobranchial gland
  • Position – Near oesophagus/posterior pharyngeal region
  • Function – Secretes calcitonin; regulates calcium metabolism (lowers blood Ca²⁺)
  • Pineal organ
  • Position – Dorsal side of brain (epithalamus)
  • Function – Secretes melatonin; controls biological rhythms, photoperiodism
  • reproduction
  • Chromaffin tissues
  • Position – Associated with kidney (head kidney/interrenal tissue)
  • Function – Secretes adrenaline & noradrenaline; involved in stress response
  • cardiovascular regulation
  • Pancreatic islets (Islets of Langerhans)
  • Position – Scattered in pancreas/hepatopancreas
  • Function – Secretes insulin, glucagon; regulates blood glucose metabolism
questions.final_answer: Function – Secretes insulin, glucagon; regulates blood glucose metabolism
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is invagination?
questions.solution_html:
• Invagination in embryology is the infolding of a part of a cell layer into the interior of
  • the embryo, It is a major movement during gastrulation., A region of the blastula folds
  • inward, forming a cavity. This process leads to the formation of the archenteron
  • Helps in the development of germ layers.

questions.question: Describe oviparity, viviparity and ovoviviparity in fishes.
questions.solution_html:
• Oviparity: Egg laying, Fertilization – external (mostly), Development – outside body
  • Large number of eggs, Less parental care
  • Viviparity: Live bearing, Fertilization – internal, Embryo develops inside female
  • Nourishment from mother, Fewer young, more protection
  • Ovoviviparity: Eggs retained inside female, Fertilization – internal, Development
  • inside egg within mother, Nourishment from yolk (no direct maternal supply), Young
  • released as live
questions.final_answer: released as live

questions.question: Describe the procedure of hypophysation.
questions.solution_html:
• Hypophysation (induced breeding using pituitary extract)
  • Selection of brooders – healthy, mature male & female, Collection of pituitary
  • gland – from donor fish, Preparation of extract – pituitary homogenized in
  • distilled water/saline, Dose determination – based on body weight & species
  • Injection – intramuscular/intraperitoneal, Two doses (female): Preliminary
  • (priming) doseand Final (resolving) dose, Single dose (male) – at time of female’s
  • final dose, Latency period – time between injection & spawning, Spawning –
  • natural or artificial (stripping), Fertilization – mixing eggs & milt, Incubation –
  • hatching of eggs under controlled conditions
questions.final_answer: hatching of eggs under controlled conditions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the gonadal level of control in induced maturation and spawning.
questions.solution_html:
• Target organ – Gonads (ovary & testis)
  • Steroid hormones – Estrogens (e.g., estradiol) – vitellogenesis (yolk
  • formation), Androgens – spermatogenesis, Progestogens (maturation-inducing
  • hormone, MIH) – final maturation
  • Ovary – Oocyte growth, Vitellogenesis, Final oocyte maturation, Ovulation
  • Testis - Spermatogenesis, Sperm maturation, Spermiation
  • Maturation Inducing Hormone (MIH) – Triggers germinal vesicle breakdown
  • (GVBD), Leads to final oocyte maturation
  • Feedback control – Steroids regulate pituitary & hypothalamus
  • Essay Questions

questions.question: Explain the maturity stages of male and female reproductive organs in teleosts with diagrams.

  • Stage I – Immature : Ovary – small, thin, transparent, Oocytes – oogonia, primary

  • Stage III – Maturing: Ovary – enlarged, yellowish, Oocytes – vitellogenic (yolk

questions.question: Summarise the different hormones produced by the Pituitary and Urophysis in fishes and explain their functions.
questions.solution_html:
• Summarise the different hormones produced by the pituitary and urophysis in
  • fishes and explain their functions
  • Pituitary gland (Hypophysis)
  • Adenohypophysis (Anterior pituitary)
  • Growth Hormone (GH) : Growth, protein synthesis, Regulates metabolism
  • osmoregulation
  • Prolactin (PRL): Freshwater adaptation, Ion regulation, parental behaviour
  • Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) : Stimulates thyroid gland, Controls
  • metabolism, metamorphosis
  • Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH) : Stimulates interrenal tissue, Stress
  • response
  • Gonadotropins (GTH I & GTH II) : GTH I – gametogenesis, vitellogenesis , GTH
  • II – maturation, ovulation, spermiation
  • Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH) : Pigment dispersion, Skin colour
  • regulation
questions.final_answer: regulation

• Invagination in embryology is the infolding of a part of a cell layer into the interior of
  • the embryo, It is a major movement during gastrulation., A region of the blastula folds
  • inward, forming a cavity. This process leads to the formation of the archenteron
  • Helps in the development of germ layers.
questions.final_answer: Helps in the development of germ layers
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Descibe sexual dimorphism in crabs.
questions.solution_html:
• Abdomen shape: Male – narrow, triangular, Female – broad, rounded
  • Pleopods : Male – modified , Female – well developed (egg carrying)
  • Chelipeds (claws): Male – larger, stronger, Female – smaller
  • Body size: Male – usually larger, Female – smaller (but broader abdomen)
  • Gonopores position: Male – on base of 5th walking legs, Female – on base of 3rd
  • walking legs
  • Abdominal segments: Male – fewer free segments, Female – more expanded for
  • brooding
questions.final_answer: brooding

questions.question: Describe oviparity, viviparity and ovoviviparity in fishes.
questions.solution_html:
• Oviparity: Egg laying, Fertilization – external (mostly), Development – outside body
  • Large number of eggs, Less parental care
  • Viviparity: Live bearing, Fertilization – internal, Embryo develops inside female
  • Nourishment from mother, Fewer young, more protection
  • Ovoviviparity: Eggs retained inside female, Fertilization – internal, Development
  • inside egg within mother, Nourishment from yolk (no direct maternal supply), Young
  • released as live
questions.final_answer: released as live
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the position, and functions of the Y-organs and Mandibular organs in Crustacea.
questions.solution_html:

  • Y-organ

  • Ecdysone (moulting hormone), Function – Initiates moulting (ecdysis), growth
  • Control – Inhibited by MIH from eyestalk
  • Mandibular organ
  • Position – At base of mandibles, Hormone – Methyl farnesoate, Function – Regulates

questions.question: Describe the advantages of producing monosex populations in aquaculture.
questions.solution_html:
• Faster growth – one sex grows faster (e.g., males in many fishes), Uniform size –
  • reduced size variation, Higher yield – improved production, Prevents unwanted
  • breeding – avoids overcrowding, Better feed conversion – energy used for growth
  • not reproduction, Improved management – easier culture practices, Better survival
questions.final_answer: not reproduction, Improved management – easier culture practices, Better survival

questions.question: Describe the procedure of hypophysation.
questions.solution_html:
• Hypophysation (induced breeding using pituitary extract)
  • Selection of brooders – healthy, mature male & female, Collection of pituitary
  • gland – from donor fish, Preparation of extract – pituitary homogenized in
  • distilled water/saline, Dose determination – based on body weight & species
  • Injection – intramuscular/intraperitoneal, Two doses (female): Preliminary
  • (priming) doseand Final (resolving) dose, Single dose (male) – at time of female’s
  • final dose, Latency period – time between injection & spawning, Spawning –
  • natural or artificial (stripping), Fertilization – mixing eggs & milt, Incubation –
  • hatching of eggs under controlled conditions
questions.final_answer: hatching of eggs under controlled conditions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the gonadal level of control in induced maturation and spawning.
questions.solution_html:
• Target organ – Gonads (ovary & testis)
  • Steroid hormones – Estrogens (e.g., estradiol) – vitellogenesis (yolk
  • formation), Androgens – spermatogenesis, Progestogens (maturation-inducing
  • hormone, MIH) – final maturation
  • Ovary – Oocyte growth, Vitellogenesis, Final oocyte maturation, Ovulation
  • Testis - Spermatogenesis, Sperm maturation, Spermiation
  • Maturation Inducing Hormone (MIH) – Triggers germinal vesicle breakdown
  • (GVBD), Leads to final oocyte maturation
  • Feedback control – Steroids regulate pituitary & hypothalamus
  • Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Essay Questions

questions.question: Explain the maturity stages of male and female reproductive organs in teleosts with diagrams.
questions.solution_html:
• Female maturity stages
  • Stage I – Immature : Ovary – small, thin, transparent, Oocytes – oogonia, primary
  • oocytes, No yolk , Thin thread-like ovary
  • Stage II – Early maturing: Ovary – slightly enlarged, Oocytes – previtellogenic
  • Beginning of cytoplasmic growth, Slightly enlarged ovary
  • Stage III – Maturing: Ovary – enlarged, yellowish, Oocytes – vitellogenic (yolk
  • deposition), Yolk vesicles present, Enlarged ovary with yolk
questions.final_answer: deposition), Yolk vesicles present, Enlarged ovary with yolk

questions.question: Summarise the different hormones produced by the Pituitary and Urophysis in fishes and explain their functions.
questions.solution_html:
• Summarise the different hormones produced by the pituitary and urophysis in
  • fishes and explain their functions
  • Pituitary gland (Hypophysis)
  • Adenohypophysis (Anterior pituitary)
  • Growth Hormone (GH) : Growth, protein synthesis, Regulates metabolism
  • osmoregulation
  • Prolactin (PRL): Freshwater adaptation, Ion regulation, parental behaviour
  • Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) : Stimulates thyroid gland, Controls
  • metabolism, metamorphosis
  • Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH) : Stimulates interrenal tissue, Stress
  • response
  • Gonadotropins (GTH I & GTH II) : GTH I – gametogenesis, vitellogenesis , GTH
  • II – maturation, ovulation, spermiation
  • Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH) : Pigment dispersion, Skin colour
  • regulation
questions.final_answer: regulation
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
